sprints.title: Service Management FY26Q3-1
sprints.goals: This sprint aimed to enhance the Intake and Fulfillment incident management systems by improving data field accessibility and workflow automation, while strengthening security controls and enabling better post-submission record management.
sprints.summary: The team completed eleven improvements across both Intake and Fulfillment systems, focusing on streamlining incident workflows and operational data integrity. Key accomplishments include resolving data field visibility issues in Intake, implementing security controls for incident records through refined access lists, automating contact lookups for incident assignment, and enabling flexible work note editing after submission. These enhancements collectively improve system usability, reduce manual data entry errors, and provide teams with greater flexibility in managing incidents and maintenance records throughout their lifecycle.

sprints.title: Service Management FY26Q3-2
sprints.goals: This sprint focused on expanding asset management capabilities across multiple systems by enhancing data models, improving user interfaces, and establishing security foundations for new pilot initiatives. The team aimed to increase operational visibility and control by modernizing how asset information is captured, displayed, and protected across Intake, SPM, and Fulfillment platforms.
sprints.summary: The team completed six substantial initiatives that strengthen asset lifecycle management and system interoperability. Work included updates to Intake asset records to reflect component-level maintenance and service life tracking, enhancements to the Fulfillment workspace to display more comprehensive asset information, and delivery of a vessel graphical dashboard that provides intuitive operational visibility. Additionally, the team designed and implemented access control architecture for the SPM pilot program, ensuring secure transition to production use. These improvements directly enable field teams to make faster, more informed decisions about asset maintenance and operations while establishing the security and data governance needed to scale new capabilities across the enterprise.

sprints.title: Service Management FY26Q3-3
sprints.goals: This sprint focused on enhancing asset management capabilities across the Intake and Fulfillment platforms by expanding data fields and reporting visibility. The work aimed to improve operational tracking of vehicle assets and provide leadership with better visibility into ticket resolution trends.
sprints.summary: The team completed six features that strengthen asset lifecycle management and reporting across both systems. Vehicle and consumable assets now capture initial hours and miles data, with improved navigation and configuration options in NavHub GEN II and the Asset Config Workspace. In parallel, performance analytics were configured to track open ticket trends, giving operations and leadership real-time insight into support backlog health. These enhancements enable more accurate asset valuation, better maintenance planning, and data-driven decision making around support resource allocation.
